absorption: Upstream provides equivalent configurable canonical peer aliases plus server-fixed identity with coverage across peer/session/message write paths.

consumers.name: ChatGPT and other clients sharing the Node MCP tool layer.

contract: Historical ChatGPT/user peer aliases are canonicalized at every shared MCP write boundary, while deployment configuration fixes trusted human/assistant defaults rather than letting callers redefine server identity.

proof.fork_expected: alias/config tests pass and integration calls converge historical aliases to their canonical peer IDs.
upstream: inspect peer/session/message identity handling on the recorded upstream base.
proof.upstream_expected: historical aliases can reach shared write boundaries without canonicalization and caller identity is not fixed by the same deployment policy.

upstream_gap: The recorded upstream base accepts caller-provided peer IDs without the fork's configurable canonical aliases and fixed deployment identity boundary.
